text.title: Ramp Task Difficulty Ladder: Failure Modes
text.summary: 6 known failure modes when running a ramp-task difficulty ladder for new developers. Each carries a detector (what to look for) and a repair (the corrective action).

failure-mode.description: Rungs by estimate: the ladder maps rungs to story points or "easy / medium / hard", so a 2-point ticket that touches billing and the deploy pipeline lands on rung 2.
failure-mode.detector: `Ticket pattern` column contains points, sizes or adjectives instead of scope (files, modules, flag, design review); two buddies place the same ticket on different rungs.
failure-mode.repair: Rewrite every rung's pattern as observable scope (`r-rung-defined-by-observable-scope`); re-classify the currently tagged tickets against the new patterns.

failure-mode.description: Sandbox rung 1: the first task is a kata or a training repo, so the newcomer's first real PR against main lands in week two or three.
failure-mode.detector: Rung 1 evidence link is not a merged PR on the production repo; `time_to_first_pr` median above 3 working days.
failure-mode.repair: Replace rung 1 with real merge-to-main changes (docs fix, dependency bump, log line) that run the full pipeline (`r-rung1-merges-to-main`).

failure-mode.description: Rung skip: the sprint is behind, the newcomer is "senior", and the buddy hands them a rung-4 migration on day two; the newcomer spends the week reverse-engineering the deploy pipeline.
failure-mode.detector: Newcomer's first merged ticket is labelled rung 3 or higher; or a ticket runs past twice its expected upper bound with no re-classification recorded.
failure-mode.repair: Enforce one merged ticket per rung before promotion and re-label overrun tickets instead of grading the hire (`r-promotion-requires-completed-rung`).

failure-mode.description: Cannibalised ramp backlog: reserved ramp tickets sat on the sprint critical path, a senior engineer pulled them when the sprint slipped, and the newcomer's day one is spent watching the buddy scroll the backlog.
failure-mode.detector: Fewer than 2 open tickets per rung carry the rung label on the start date; rung-1/2 tickets carry a sprint deadline inside the ramp window.
failure-mode.repair: Tag at least 2 tickets per rung before the start date and keep rungs 1 and 2 off the committed sprint scope (`r-tickets-tagged-before-start-date`).

failure-mode.description: Support that does not fade: the buddy pairs full-time through rung 5, or drops to nothing at rung 2; the newcomer either cannot work alone after the ramp or stalls silently for three days.
failure-mode.detector: `Buddy support` column is identical across rungs, non-monotonic, or reads "none" inside the ramp window; newcomer has no merged PR for 3 or more days with no buddy contact logged.
failure-mode.repair: Set full pairing at rung 1 and scheduled check-ins only at the top rung, strictly decreasing between (`r-buddy-support-fades-per-rung`).

failure-mode.description: Whiteboard durations: the duration bands were invented by people who know the codebase, no rung has a prior completed ramp behind it, and every newcomer looks slow against them; the outcome review never regrades.
failure-mode.detector: Evidence links point at unstarted backlog items or senior engineers' PRs; a rung's median actual duration sits outside its band for two consecutive reviews with no version bump.
failure-mode.repair: Mark unvalidated rungs `not_applicable: unvalidated` until a real ramp fills them (`r-evidence-is-a-completed-prior-ramp`); re-band from actual durations at the outcome review and bump the version (`r-outcome-review-regrades-rungs`).
